title: Landscaping CRM: 6 Tools to Track Leads and Repeat Work
html:
A landscaping CRM should track every lead, bid and repeat customer in one place. Start with a free sales CRM or a field service app with client records, and add landscaping CRM automation once follow-ups slip. Published plans here run from free to $648 a month. SynkedUP publishes no price at all.

A landscaping CRM has two jobs: win the bid and bring the customer back next season. Most landscaping revenue repeats. A spring cleanup customer becomes a mowing customer, and a patio client becomes a lighting client. A spreadsheet loses those threads by July. This guide compares six tools by how they hold leads and clients, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit.

Some tools are general CRMs and some are landscape business apps with a CRM inside. They solve different problems, so the guide groups them that way.

Which landscaping CRM is free to start?

HubSpot and Zoho both list a free CRM tier, so a landscaper can track bids for nothing before paying for anything.

  • HubSpot CRM: a general sales CRM with a free tier. The vendor lists it as free for up to 2 users with no credit card. Limit: the free tier holds 1,000 contacts. The paid Starter plan is $20 per seat a month, with a limited-time discount for new customers.
  • Zoho CRM: a sales CRM with a free plan for up to 3 users. Limit: the free plan allows 10 custom email templates, 10 data exports and 5,000 API calls a day. Paid plans are priced per user, and the page shows currency by region, so check the vendor for your figure.

A free CRM suits an owner who bids every job. You log each lead, set a follow-up date and mark the bid won or lost. It does not route crews or send invoices, so you still run the work somewhere else.

The 1,000 contact cap is easy to pass in a mowing business that keeps every property. Export the list each quarter so a later move to another tool takes an hour, not a week.

Which landscaping CRM also schedules crews and invoices?

Jobber, LMN and Service Fusion keep client records next to scheduling, estimates and invoices. That suits a landscaper who wants one tool.

  • Jobber: a field service app with client records, quotes, scheduling and invoicing. The Core plan for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and card processing is 2.9% plus 30 cents.
  • LMN: a landscape business app with a landscaper-designed CRM and a customer portal, plus budgeting, estimating, scheduling and invoicing. Starter is $297 a month billed monthly, and Professional is $648 a month. Limit: both plans carry a one-time onboarding fee, and extra licenses cost more.
  • Service Fusion: customer management, estimates, scheduling, dispatching and invoicing. Starter is $208 a month billed annually or $245 billed monthly, with unlimited users and month to month terms. Limit: the page lists customer management but shows no detail on CRM depth.

LMN is the heaviest of the three. A $297 plan plus onboarding makes sense for a firm that budgets every job. A route-based mowing business should start with Jobber or Service Fusion.

Which landscaping CRM fits lead intake and estimating?

A firm that sells bigger projects needs lead intake tied to estimating, so a request becomes a priced bid without retyping.

Ask for a demo with your own price list. A template bid hides how the tool handles a real patio or a drainage job. Also ask how a lead from your website form reaches the CRM.

How do the six landscaping CRM tools compare?

The table puts the published facts side by side so you can see where each tool starts and where it stops.

ToolPublished entry priceUsersMain limit
HubSpot CRMFree, Starter listed at $20 a seat a monthUp to 2 on free1,000 contacts on free
Zoho CRMFree plan, paid prices vary by regionUp to 3 on free10 data exports on free
Jobber$29 a month billed annually, $49 with no commitment1 on CoreExtra users cost $29 a month
LMN$297 a month billed monthly1 office, 5 crew licensesOne-time onboarding fee
Service Fusion$208 a month billed annuallyUnlimitedCRM depth not shown
SynkedUPNot publishedNot shownNo published price

Source: each vendor's own pages, read in November 2026. Prices exclude tax, card processing fees and onboarding fees.

Read the table by business type. An owner who bids alone should start free. A route-based crew should price Jobber or Service Fusion. A firm that budgets projects should price LMN or SynkedUP.

When does a landscaper outgrow a spreadsheet?

A landscaper outgrows a spreadsheet when bids go unanswered because no one remembers who asked. The cost shows up as lost jobs, not as a line on a bill.

  • Missed follow-ups: if you cannot say which bids are waiting on a reply, you are losing work you already earned.
  • Repeat customers: if spring cleanup clients are not offered mowing in summer, a CRM would pay for itself quickly.
  • More than one estimator: two people editing one sheet leads to overwritten notes and double calls.

Until one of those shows up, a free CRM is plenty. The goal is a habit of logging every lead on the day it arrives, not a bigger tool.

How should a landscaper set up CRM pipeline stages?

Use six stages that match how landscaping work moves: new request, site visit, bid sent, follow-up, won or lost, and renewal.

  1. New request. Log the source, the service and the property address.
  2. Site visit. Move the lead only when a visit date is set.
  3. Bid sent. Attach the written price and set a follow-up date before you leave the screen.
  4. Follow-up. Call after two days and again after a week, and note each reply.
  5. Won or lost. Record the reason for every loss, such as price, timing or a competitor.
  6. Renewal. Set a reminder for next season, so spring cleanups turn into mowing contracts.

The renewal stage is where landscaping differs from most trades. A customer you serve in one season is the cheapest lead you will get in the next. Set the reminder on the day the job closes.

Review lost reasons each quarter. If most losses say price, change how you present the bid. If they say timing, your follow-up is too slow.

What should a landscaper test in a CRM trial?

Test how fast you answer a new request, not how clean the dashboard looks.

  • Capture: send a test request from your website form and see whether it lands in the CRM without retyping.
  • Reminders: set a follow-up for two days out and confirm your phone alerts you.
  • Mobile use: log a lead from a job site in under a minute.
  • Export: download your full client list as a file, so you know you can leave.

Import last year's clients too. A CRM full of past customers lets you call people who asked for a bid last spring and never heard a no. Test with the busiest month in mind, since the tool must hold up in April.

What does a landscaping CRM stack cost per month?

A small landscaping stack can cost $0 for the CRM. A business app runs about $29 to $648 a month, using only the published prices above.

  • Solo landscaper: HubSpot or Zoho free tier plus a free Google Business Profile.
  • Two-truck crew: Jobber Core at $29 a month billed annually, plus $29 for a second user.
  • Growing crew: Service Fusion Starter at $208 a month billed annually covers unlimited users.
  • Project firm: LMN Starter at $297 a month billed monthly, or Professional at $648, plus onboarding.

These figures cover the software only. Card processing, onboarding and add-ons sit on top. Compare the total with one average job, and shrink the plan if it costs more than a week of work.

Seasonal pricing matters in this trade. Ask each vendor whether you can pause or downgrade in winter, and get the answer in writing. A plan you cannot shrink costs the same in January as in May.

Plan for the cost of switching, too. Moving client records and bids to a new app takes real hours. Pick a tool you can live with for two years.

What does a landscaping CRM not do?

A CRM stores leads. It does not create them, so a full pipeline still depends on search, maps, reviews and ads.

  • Google Business Profile: the free listing that puts a landscaping company on Google Maps. Google states that creating a Business Profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it needs fresh project photos and review replies to rank near the top.

Past clients are worth an email marketing follow-up each season, and remarketing keeps your name in front of people who viewed a bid page.

How do you choose a landscaping CRM?

Choose a landscaping CRM with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it track bids, follow-up dates and renewals, and can you see every lead by source?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users, onboarding and card fees, then compare the total with one average job.

Setup effort: can one person import your client list and build the pipeline in a weekend?

A solo landscaper can run on a free HubSpot or Zoho plan. A route-based crew fits Jobber or Service Fusion. A firm that budgets projects should price LMN and SynkedUP side by side.

What is the best CRM for a landscaping company?

There is no single best, because it depends on how you sell. A solo owner can start with HubSpot or Zoho, which both list a free tier. A route-based crew should price Jobber or Service Fusion. A firm that budgets projects should price LMN. Test each on real bids.

Is there a free CRM for landscapers?

Yes. HubSpot lists a free CRM for up to 2 users with a 1,000 contact limit, and Zoho lists a free plan for up to 3 users. Both are general sales CRMs, so they do not route crews or send invoices. You would pair them with a business app later.

How much does a landscaping CRM cost?

Published plans in this guide run from free to $648 a month. Jobber Core starts at $29 a month on annual billing, Service Fusion Starter at $208, and LMN Starter at $297 with an onboarding fee. SynkedUP publishes no price, so ask for a quote.

What should a landscaper track in a CRM?

Track the lead source, service, bid amount, follow-up date, loss reason and renewal date. Those fields show which channel pays, how fast you follow up and which customers should return next season. Renewal dates matter most in a seasonal trade.

Can a CRM get a landscaper more leads?

No. A CRM organizes leads you already have and helps you follow up faster. New leads come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A free Google Business Profile, a site with project photos and paid search put your number in front of homeowners first.

How long does it take to set up a landscaping CRM?

A free CRM with six pipeline stages takes a few hours to set up and a weekend to fill with past clients. Business apps take longer because of price lists and routes. Start the trial before the season so you can finish the import.

does it track bids, follow-up dates and renewals, and can you see every lead by source?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra users, onboarding and card fees, then compare the total with one average job.
Setup effort:
can one person import your client list and build the pipeline in a weekend?
A solo landscaper can run on a free HubSpot or Zoho plan. A route-based crew fits Jobber or Service Fusion. A firm that budgets projects should price LMN and SynkedUP side by side.
###
What is the best CRM for a landscaping company?
There is no single best, because it depends on how you sell. A solo owner can start with HubSpot or Zoho, which both list a free tier. A route-based crew should price Jobber or Service Fusion. A firm that budgets projects should price LMN. Test each on real bids.
###
Is there a free CRM for landscapers?
Yes. HubSpot lists a free CRM for up to 2 users with a 1,000 contact limit, and Zoho lists a free plan for up to 3 users. Both are general sales CRMs, so they do not route crews or send invoices. You would pair them with a business app later.
###
How much does a landscaping CRM cost?
Published plans in this guide run from free to $648 a month. Jobber Core starts at $29 a month on annual billing, Service Fusion Starter at $208, and LMN Starter at $297 with an onboarding fee. SynkedUP publishes no price, so ask for a quote.
###
What should a landscaper track in a CRM?
Track the lead source, service, bid amount, follow-up date, loss reason and renewal date. Those fields show which channel pays, how fast you follow up and which customers should return next season. Renewal dates matter most in a seasonal trade.
###
Can a CRM get a landscaper more leads?
No. A CRM organizes leads you already have and helps you follow up faster. New leads come from search, maps, reviews and ads. A free Google Business Profile, a site with project photos and paid search put your number in front of homeowners first.
###
How long does it take to set up a landscaping CRM?
A free CRM with six pipeline stages takes a few hours to set up and a weekend to fill with past clients. Business apps take longer because of price lists and routes. Start the trial before the season so you can finish the import.
